projects.title: Formalizing Limits of Obedience in Autonomous Systems

review.alternative: Catastrophic outcomes may stem from hardware failures or malicious actors rather than directive compliance.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that agent autonomous decisions in high-stakes domains consistently prioritize safety over explicit, potentially harmful directives.

claims.statement: Strict directive adherence in autonomous systems can lead to catastrophic failure when the directive conflicts with safety parameters in high-stakes scenarios like CBRN domains.

support.explanation: This establishes the context of catastrophic risk arising from the autonomy of LLMs in high-stakes domains.
support.passage: Large language models (LLMs) are evolving into autonomous decision-makers, raising concerns about catastrophic risks in high-stakes scenarios, particularly in Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) domains.

support.explanation: Confirms the scope of research into catastrophic outcomes resulting from agent decision-making.
support.passage: Nuclear Deployed: Analyzing Catastrophic Risks in Decision-making of Autonomous LLM Agents
